# Read Me: How to use this file

This RMD was constructed for partial data analysis during the preparation of [FILL IN MANUSCRIPT TITLE]. The workflows in this file are intended to estimate the potential epidemiological impact that vultures may have during an anthrax outbreak, through removal of biomass from large mammal carcasses.

**Before running this pipeline, you will need:**

- A carcass pool dataset with pool IDs, coordinates (UTM recommended), and total dead counts per pool
- A vulture GPS dataset with bird IDs, timestamps, and location coordinates
- R packages: `dplyr`, `sf`, `readr`, `ggplot2`, `scales`, `tidyr`

**User-defined inputs to update before running:**

- `DATADIR`: path to your data directory
- File names for your carcass and vulture datasets
- `DIST_THRESHOLD`: your chosen distance threshold (m) for classifying a foraging visit
- `D`: your analysis window in days
- Body mass and intake rate assumptions appropriate for your study species

---

## Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(tidyr)

# ── USER-DEFINED INPUTS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Set your data directory
DATADIR <- "path/to/your/data/directory"

# Distance threshold (m) for classifying a GPS fix as a foraging visit
# We used 500m for white-backed vultures at hippo carcass pools
DIST_THRESHOLD <- 500

# Analysis window in days
# Set to your outbreak period + any post-outbreak buffer you wish to include
D <- 103  # e.g., 73-day outbreak + 30-day post-outbreak buffer

# ── BODY MASS SCENARIOS (kg per carcass) ─────────────────────────────────────
# Replace with values appropriate for your study species
# Low:  lower bound estimate (cite source)
# Mid:  midpoint (average of low and high)
# High: upper bound estimate (cite source)
M_low  <- 0000.0   # e.g., Eltringham 1999 for hippo
M_mid  <- 0000.0
M_high <- 0000.0

# ── DAILY VULTURE INTAKE SCENARIOS (kg/vulture/day) ──────────────────────────
# Replace with values appropriate for your study species
# Low:  conservative estimate (cite source)
# Mid:  midpoint field estimate (cite source)
# High: upper bound estimate (cite source)
U_low  <- 0.000   # e.g., Houston 1976
U_mid  <- 0.000   # e.g., Ruxton & Houston 2002
U_high <- 0.000   # e.g., Brink et al. 2020
```

---

# Step 1: Calculate vulture distance to each carcass pool

**Purpose:** Identify GPS fixes that fall within your chosen distance threshold of each carcass pool, and use these to classify foraging visits.

**Determine a meaningful visit distance threshold** for your study species that would constitute a foraging visit (e.g., we used <500 m for white-backed vultures at hippo carcass pools). Match birds to pools using UTM coordinates rather than lat/long to avoid coordinate distortion errors.

**Archetype definitions used in this pipeline:**

| Archetype | Definition |
|---|---|
| Super user | ≥100 total within-threshold GPS fixes |
| Moderate user | <100 total within-threshold fixes AND ≥3 unique pools visited |
| Limited user | 1–2 unique pools visited |
| Non user | 0 within-threshold fixes at any pool |

*Adjust these thresholds to suit your data and study system.*

**Datasets needed:**
- Carcass pool file: pool IDs, UTM coordinates (or lat/long for conversion), total dead per pool
- Vulture GPS file: bird IDs, timestamps, location coordinates

```{r step1-load-pools}
# ── LOAD CARCASS POOL COORDINATES ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Replace "your_carcass_pool_file.csv" with your file name
# Required columns: pool ID, UTM x, UTM y (or lat/long), total dead
carcass_pools <- read_csv(
  file.path(DATADIR, "your_carcass_pool_file.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(utm_x)) %>%            # remove rows with missing coordinates
  transmute(
    pool_id    = pool_id_column,        # replace with your pool ID column name
    pool_utm_x = utm_x_column,          # replace with your UTM x column name
    pool_utm_y = utm_y_column,          # replace with your UTM y column name
    total_dead = total_dead_column      # replace with your dead count column name
  )

cat("=== CARCASS POOLS ===\n")
print(carcass_pools)
cat("Total pools:", nrow(carcass_pools), "\n")
cat("Total dead across all pools:", sum(carcass_pools$total_dead), "\n")
```

```{r step1-verify-coordinates}
# ── OPTIONAL: VERIFY UTM COORDINATES AGAINST LAT/LONG CONVERSION ──────────────
# If you have both UTM and lat/long stored, verify they match
# Skip this block if you only have one coordinate format

# Build pool sf from stored UTM
pools_sf_utm <- carcass_pools %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("pool_utm_x", "pool_utm_y"), crs = 32736)  # update EPSG for your UTM zone

# Build pool sf from lat/long and convert to UTM
pools_sf_latlong <- carcass_pools %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("pool_lon", "pool_lat"), crs = 4326) %>%   # update if column names differ
  st_transform(32736)                                              # update EPSG for your UTM zone

# Compare stored vs derived UTM — should be <1m difference if coordinates are correct
coords_stored  <- st_coordinates(pools_sf_utm)
coords_derived <- st_coordinates(pools_sf_latlong)

verification <- carcass_pools %>%
  select(pool_id, pool_utm_x, pool_utm_y) %>%
  mutate(
    derived_utm_x = coords_derived[, 1],
    derived_utm_y = coords_derived[, 2],
    diff_x_m      = abs(pool_utm_x - derived_utm_x),
    diff_y_m      = abs(pool_utm_y - derived_utm_y)
  )

cat("=== UTM VERIFICATION: STORED vs DERIVED FROM LAT/LONG ===\n")
print(verification)
cat("Max X difference (m):", max(verification$diff_x_m), "\n")
cat("Max Y difference (m):", max(verification$diff_y_m), "\n")
```

```{r step1-load-vultures}
# ── LOAD VULTURE GPS DATA ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Replace "your_vulture_gps_file.csv" with your file name
# Required columns: bird ID, timestamp, longitude, latitude
vulture_df <- read_csv(
  file.path(DATADIR, "your_vulture_gps_file.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  transmute(
    bird_id    = bird_id_column,              # replace with your bird ID column name
    date       = as.Date(timestamp_column),   # replace with your timestamp column name
    lon        = longitude_column,            # replace with your longitude column name
    lat        = latitude_column              # replace with your latitude column name
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lon), !is.na(lat))

cat("=== VULTURE GPS DATA ===\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(vulture_df), "\n")
cat("Unique birds:", n_distinct(vulture_df$bird_id), "\n")
cat("Date range:", as.character(min(vulture_df$date)),
    "to", as.character(max(vulture_df$date)), "\n")

# NOTE: Check your date range against your outbreak window.
# If your GPS data starts after outbreak onset, note this as a limitation —
# removal estimates will be conservative lower bounds for the uncovered period.
```

```{r step1-calculate-distances}
# ── CONVERT VULTURE POINTS TO UTM ─────────────────────────────────────────────
vulture_sf <- vulture_df %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(32736)   # update EPSG to match your UTM zone

# ── CALCULATE DISTANCES: EVERY VULTURE FIX TO EVERY POOL ─────────────────────
cat("Calculating distances from all GPS fixes to all pools...\n")

results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pools_sf_utm)), function(i) {
  dists <- as.numeric(st_distance(vulture_sf, pools_sf_utm[i, ]))
  vulture_df %>%
    mutate(
      pool_id        = carcass_pools$pool_id[i],
      total_dead     = carcass_pools$total_dead[i],
      dist_m         = dists,
      within_thresh  = dist_m <= DIST_THRESHOLD
    )
}) %>% bind_rows()

cat("Distance calculation complete.\n")
```

```{r step1-summarize-visits}
# ── BIRD x POOL VISIT SUMMARY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
bird_pool_binary <- results %>%
  group_by(bird_id, pool_id, total_dead) %>%
  summarise(
    visited       = as.integer(any(within_thresh)),
    n_fixes       = sum(within_thresh),
    n_days        = n_distinct(date[within_thresh]),
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

cat("=== BIRD x POOL VISIT TABLE (visited pools only) ===\n")
print(bird_pool_binary %>% filter(visited == 1), n = Inf)

# ── ASSIGN ARCHETYPES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Adjust thresholds below to suit your data
bird_summary <- bird_pool_binary %>%
  group_by(bird_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_fixes          = sum(n_fixes),
    total_days           = sum(n_days),
    n_unique_pools       = sum(visited),
    pools_visited        = paste(sort(pool_id[visited == 1]), collapse = ", "),
    .groups              = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    archetype = case_when(
      total_fixes == 0                              ~ "Non user",
      total_fixes >= 100                            ~ "Super user",      # adjust threshold
      n_unique_pools >= 3 & total_fixes < 100       ~ "Moderate user",   # adjust thresholds
      n_unique_pools %in% c(1, 2)                   ~ "Limited user",
      TRUE                                          ~ "Limited user"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_fixes))

cat("\n=== PER-BIRD SUMMARY WITH ARCHETYPES ===\n")
print(bird_summary, n = Inf)

# ── SAVE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_csv(bird_pool_binary, file.path(DATADIR, "output_bird_pool_visit_binary.csv"))
write_csv(bird_summary,     file.path(DATADIR, "output_bird_summary_archetypes.csv"))
cat("\nSaved: output_bird_pool_visit_binary.csv\n")
cat("Saved: output_bird_summary_archetypes.csv\n")
```

---

# Step 2: Estimate pool biomass and model vulture removal

**Purpose:** Calculate total carcass biomass per pool under three body-mass scenarios, then model how much biomass each tagged bird could have removed based on their GPS-derived foraging visit patterns.

**Key assumption:** Biomass removal is credited on days a bird records at least one within-threshold GPS fix. Daily removal is capped at the scenario-specific intake rate and allocated across pools in proportion to within-threshold fix counts.

```{r step2-pool-biomass}
# ── TOTAL BIOMASS PER POOL ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool_biomass <- carcass_pools %>%
  mutate(
    biomass_low  = total_dead * M_low,
    biomass_mid  = total_dead * M_mid,
    biomass_high = total_dead * M_high
  )

cat("=== TOTAL BIOMASS PER POOL ===\n")
print(pool_biomass)

cat("\n=== TOTAL OUTBREAK BIOMASS (ALL POOLS) ===\n")
cat("Low:  ", sum(pool_biomass$biomass_low),  "kg\n")
cat("Mid:  ", sum(pool_biomass$biomass_mid),  "kg\n")
cat("High: ", sum(pool_biomass$biomass_high), "kg\n")
```

```{r step2-model-removal}
# ── MODELED VULTURE REMOVAL PER BIRD PER POOL ─────────────────────────────────
# Total visit-days per bird across all pools
bird_total_days <- bird_pool_binary %>%
  group_by(bird_id) %>%
  summarise(total_visit_days = sum(n_days), .groups = "drop")

# Allocate removal across pools proportional to within-threshold fix counts
bird_pool_removal <- bird_pool_binary %>%
  left_join(bird_total_days, by = "bird_id") %>%
  mutate(
    visit_share  = ifelse(total_visit_days > 0, n_days / total_visit_days, 0),
    removal_low  = visit_share * U_low  * total_visit_days,
    removal_mid  = visit_share * U_mid  * total_visit_days,
    removal_high = visit_share * U_high * total_visit_days
  )

cat("=== MODELED REMOVAL PER BIRD PER POOL (active pools only) ===\n")
print(bird_pool_removal %>%
        filter(n_days > 0) %>%
        select(bird_id, pool_id, n_days, visit_share,
               removal_low, removal_mid, removal_high),
      n = Inf)
```

```{r step2-pool-summary}
# ── REMAINING BIOMASS PER POOL ────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool_removal_total <- bird_pool_removal %>%
  group_by(pool_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_removal_low  = sum(removal_low,  na.rm = TRUE),
    total_removal_mid  = sum(removal_mid,  na.rm = TRUE),
    total_removal_high = sum(removal_high, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pool_q1_summary <- pool_biomass %>%
  left_join(pool_removal_total, by = "pool_id") %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("total_removal"), ~replace_na(., 0)),
    remaining_low  = pmax(0, biomass_low  - total_removal_low),
    remaining_mid  = pmax(0, biomass_mid  - total_removal_mid),
    remaining_high = pmax(0, biomass_high - total_removal_high)
  )

cat("=== FULL POOL SUMMARY: BIOMASS INPUT, REMOVAL, REMAINING ===\n")
print(pool_q1_summary, n = Inf)

cat("\n=== TOTALS ACROSS ALL POOLS (midpoint scenario) ===\n")
cat("Total biomass input:    ", sum(pool_q1_summary$biomass_mid),       "kg\n")
cat("Total modeled removal:  ", sum(pool_q1_summary$total_removal_mid),  "kg\n")
cat("Total remaining:        ", sum(pool_q1_summary$remaining_mid),      "kg\n")
cat("Percent removed:        ",
    round(100 * sum(pool_q1_summary$total_removal_mid) /
            sum(pool_q1_summary$biomass_mid), 2), "%\n")

# ── SAVE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_csv(pool_biomass,      file.path(DATADIR, "output_pool_biomass_totals.csv"))
write_csv(pool_q1_summary,   file.path(DATADIR, "output_pool_biomass_removal_summary.csv"))
write_csv(bird_pool_removal, file.path(DATADIR, "output_bird_pool_removal.csv"))
cat("\nSaved: output_pool_biomass_totals.csv\n")
cat("Saved: output_pool_biomass_removal_summary.csv\n")
cat("Saved: output_bird_pool_removal.csv\n")
```

---

# Step 3: Archetype-level removal and descriptive correlations

**Purpose:** Summarize modeled biomass removal by behavioral archetype, add a hypothetical daily carcass user as a theoretical upper bound, and describe the association between use-intensity metrics and removal potential using Spearman rank correlation. Given small sample sizes typical of GPS tracking studies, this is treated as a descriptive analysis rather than a formal statistical test.

```{r step3-archetype-removal}
# ── PER-BIRD REMOVAL TOTALS BY ARCHETYPE ──────────────────────────────────────
B_low  <- sum(pool_q1_summary$biomass_low)
B_mid  <- sum(pool_q1_summary$biomass_mid)
B_high <- sum(pool_q1_summary$biomass_high)

bird_archetype_removal <- bird_summary %>%
  select(bird_id, total_fixes, total_days, n_unique_pools, archetype) %>%
  mutate(
    total_removal_low  = total_days * U_low,
    total_removal_mid  = total_days * U_mid,
    total_removal_high = total_days * U_high,
    pct_days_active    = round(100 * total_days / D, 1)
  )

cat("=== PER-BIRD ARCHETYPE REMOVAL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(bird_archetype_removal, n = Inf)

# ── ARCHETYPE-LEVEL SUMMARY ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
archetype_summary <- bird_archetype_removal %>%
  group_by(archetype) %>%
  summarise(
    n_birds              = n(),
    mean_fixes           = round(mean(total_fixes), 1),
    mean_days_active     = round(mean(total_days), 1),
    mean_removal_low_kg  = round(mean(total_removal_low), 2),
    mean_removal_mid_kg  = round(mean(total_removal_mid), 2),
    mean_removal_high_kg = round(mean(total_removal_high), 2),
    total_removal_low_kg = round(sum(total_removal_low), 2),
    total_removal_mid_kg = round(sum(total_removal_mid), 2),
    total_removal_high_kg= round(sum(total_removal_high), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_removal_mid_kg))

cat("\n=== ARCHETYPE-LEVEL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(archetype_summary, n = Inf)

cat("\n=== ARCHETYPE REMOVAL AS % OF TOTAL OUTBREAK BIOMASS ===\n")
archetype_summary %>%
  mutate(
    pct_removed_low  = round(100 * total_removal_low_kg  / B_low,  3),
    pct_removed_mid  = round(100 * total_removal_mid_kg  / B_mid,  3),
    pct_removed_high = round(100 * total_removal_high_kg / B_high, 3)
  ) %>%
  select(archetype, n_birds, total_removal_mid_kg,
         pct_removed_low, pct_removed_mid, pct_removed_high) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r step3-hypothetical-user}
# ── ADD HYPOTHETICAL DAILY CARCASS USER ───────────────────────────────────────
# This represents a bird present at a carcass pool on every day of the
# analysis window — a theoretical upper bound on individual removal capacity.
# Adjust n_unique_pools to match the pools actually visited in your data.

bird_q3 <- bird_summary %>%
  select(bird_id, total_fixes, total_days, n_unique_pools, pools_visited, archetype) %>%
  mutate(
    total_removal_low_kg  = total_days * U_low,
    total_removal_mid_kg  = total_days * U_mid,
    total_removal_high_kg = total_days * U_high,
    pct_days_active       = round(100 * total_days / D, 1),
    pct_biomass_removed_mid = round(100 * total_removal_mid_kg / B_mid, 4),
    is_hypothetical       = FALSE
  )

hypothetical_daily <- tibble(
  bird_id               = NA_real_,
  total_fixes           = D,
  total_days            = D,
  n_unique_pools        = NA_integer_,  # update with number of pools your vultures visited
  pools_visited         = "update with pool IDs your vultures used",
  archetype             = "Hypothetical daily user",
  total_removal_low_kg  = D * U_low,
  total_removal_mid_kg  = D * U_mid,
  total_removal_high_kg = D * U_high,
  pct_days_active       = 100,
  pct_biomass_removed_mid = round(100 * (D * U_mid) / B_mid, 4),
  is_hypothetical       = TRUE
)

bird_q3_full <- bind_rows(bird_q3, hypothetical_daily)

cat("=== FULL BIRD ARCHETYPE REMOVAL TABLE (including hypothetical user) ===\n")
print(bird_q3_full %>%
        select(bird_id, archetype, total_fixes, total_days,
               n_unique_pools, pct_days_active,
               total_removal_low_kg, total_removal_mid_kg,
               total_removal_high_kg, pct_biomass_removed_mid),
      n = Inf)
```

```{r step3-correlations}
# ── DESCRIPTIVE SPEARMAN CORRELATIONS ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Spearman rank correlation used given small sample sizes and because
# the active-days metric is structurally linked to modeled removal.
# Results are descriptive only — not formal statistical tests.

obs_birds <- bird_q3 %>% filter(!is_hypothetical)

cor_fixes  <- cor(obs_birds$total_fixes,      obs_birds$total_removal_mid_kg, method = "spearman")
cor_days   <- cor(obs_birds$total_days,        obs_birds$total_removal_mid_kg, method = "spearman")
cor_pools  <- cor(obs_birds$n_unique_pools,    obs_birds$total_removal_mid_kg, method = "spearman")

cat("=== DESCRIPTIVE CORRELATIONS (observed birds only) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Spearman r — total fixes vs removal (mid):      %.3f\n", cor_fixes))
cat(sprintf("Spearman r — days active vs removal (mid):      %.3f\n", cor_days))
cat(sprintf("Spearman r — unique pools vs removal (mid):     %.3f\n", cor_pools))
cat("Note: Descriptive only — not interpreted as formal statistical tests.\n")

# ── SAVE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_csv(bird_q3_full,       file.path(DATADIR, "output_bird_archetype_removal_full.csv"))
write_csv(archetype_summary,  file.path(DATADIR, "output_archetype_removal_summary.csv"))
cat("\nSaved: output_bird_archetype_removal_full.csv\n")
cat("Saved: output_archetype_removal_summary.csv\n")
```

---

# Step 4: Vultures needed to reach biomass removal thresholds

**Purpose:** Estimate how many vultures of each behavioral archetype would be required to remove 10%, 20%, and 50% of total outbreak biomass over the analysis window, assuming vultures acted as the sole scavenger guild. Run sensitivity analyses across all combinations of body-mass and intake-rate scenarios.

**Note:** Because epidemiological thresholds for scavenger-mediated carcass removal sufficient to interrupt disease transmission are unknown, these are operational reference benchmarks rather than validated epidemiological targets. Adjust threshold percentages to suit your study system.

```{r step4-setup}
# ── SCENARIO GRID ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
biomass_scenarios <- tibble(
  biomass_scenario = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
  total_biomass_kg = c(B_low, B_mid, B_high)
)

intake_scenarios <- tibble(
  intake_scenario = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
  intake_rate_kg  = c(U_low, U_mid, U_high)
)

# Adjust removal thresholds as appropriate for your study system
thresholds <- tibble(
  threshold_pct   = c(10, 20, 50),
  threshold_label = c("10%", "20%", "50%")
)

# ── ARCHETYPE MEAN ACTIVE DAYS ────────────────────────────────────────────────
archetype_days <- archetype_summary %>%
  filter(archetype != "Hypothetical daily user") %>%
  select(archetype, mean_days_active)

archetype_days <- bind_rows(
  archetype_days,
  tibble(archetype = "Hypothetical daily user", mean_days_active = as.numeric(D))
)

cat("=== ARCHETYPE MEAN ACTIVE DAYS ===\n")
print(archetype_days)
```

```{r step4-calculate}
# ── CORE CALCULATION ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# For each archetype x biomass scenario x intake scenario x threshold:
# removal per bird = mean active days x daily intake rate
# vultures needed  = ceiling(target biomass / removal per bird)
# Non users excluded (removal capacity undefined at 0 active days)

step4_results <- archetype_days %>%
  cross_join(biomass_scenarios) %>%
  cross_join(intake_scenarios)  %>%
  cross_join(thresholds)        %>%
  mutate(
    removal_per_bird_kg = mean_days_active * intake_rate_kg,
    target_removal_kg   = total_biomass_kg * (threshold_pct / 100),
    n_vultures_needed   = ifelse(
      removal_per_bird_kg == 0,
      NA_real_,
      ceiling(target_removal_kg / removal_per_bird_kg)
    ),
    total_removal_all_kg = n_vultures_needed * removal_per_bird_kg,
    actual_pct_removed   = round(100 * total_removal_all_kg / total_biomass_kg, 2)
  ) %>%
  select(archetype, mean_days_active,
         biomass_scenario, total_biomass_kg,
         intake_scenario, intake_rate_kg,
         threshold_label, threshold_pct,
         target_removal_kg, removal_per_bird_kg,
         n_vultures_needed, total_removal_all_kg, actual_pct_removed) %>%
  arrange(archetype, threshold_pct, biomass_scenario, intake_scenario)

# ── MIDPOINT SCENARIO SUMMARY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
step4_mid <- step4_results %>%
  filter(biomass_scenario == "Mid", intake_scenario == "Mid") %>%
  select(archetype, mean_days_active, threshold_label,
         target_removal_kg, removal_per_bird_kg, n_vultures_needed)

cat("=== MIDPOINT SCENARIO SUMMARY ===\n")
print(step4_mid, n = Inf)

# ── SENSITIVITY TABLE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step4_sensitivity <- step4_results %>%
  mutate(scenario_combo = paste0(biomass_scenario, " biomass | ", intake_scenario, " intake")) %>%
  select(archetype, threshold_label, scenario_combo, n_vultures_needed) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario_combo, values_from = n_vultures_needed) %>%
  arrange(archetype, threshold_label)

cat("\n=== SENSITIVITY TABLE: VULTURES NEEDED (all scenario combinations) ===\n")
print(step4_sensitivity, n = Inf)

# ── NARRATIVE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n=== NARRATIVE (midpoint scenario) ===\n")
step4_mid %>%
  filter(!is.na(n_vultures_needed)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(line = sprintf(
    "To remove %s of outbreak biomass (%.0f kg): %.0f %s birds needed | %.2f kg/bird over %.1f active days",
    threshold_label, target_removal_kg, n_vultures_needed,
    archetype, removal_per_bird_kg, mean_days_active
  )) %>%
  pull(line) %>%
  cat(sep = "\n")

# ── SAVE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
write_csv(step4_results,     file.path(DATADIR, "output_step4_vultures_needed_full.csv"))
write_csv(step4_sensitivity, file.path(DATADIR, "output_step4_sensitivity_table.csv"))
cat("\nSaved: output_step4_vultures_needed_full.csv\n")
cat("Saved: output_step4_sensitivity_table.csv\n")
```

```{r step4-plot}
# ── PLOT: VULTURES NEEDED BY ARCHETYPE AND THRESHOLD ─────────────────────────
# Colorblind-safe Okabe-Ito palette
# Update archetype_order and arch_colors to match your archetypes

archetype_order <- c("Moderate user", "Super user", "Hypothetical daily user")

arch_colors <- c(
  "Hypothetical daily user" = "#0072B2",   # blue
  "Super user"              = "#009E73",   # bluish green
  "Moderate user"           = "#E69F00"    # orange
  # Add or adjust colors for additional archetypes
)

archetype_labels <- c(
  "Hypothetical daily user" = "Hypothetical\ndaily user",
  "Super user"              = "Super user",
  "Moderate user"           = "Moderate user"
)

threshold_labeller <- as_labeller(c(
  "10%" = "10% removal",
  "20%" = "20% removal",
  "50%" = "50% removal"
  # Update labels if you use different thresholds
))

plot_data <- step4_results %>%
  filter(
    biomass_scenario == "Mid",
    intake_scenario  == "Mid",
    !is.na(n_vultures_needed),
    archetype != "Non user"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    archetype       = factor(archetype, levels = archetype_order),
    threshold_label = factor(threshold_label, levels = c("10%", "20%", "50%"))
  )

step4_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = archetype, y = n_vultures_needed, fill = archetype)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, alpha = 0.92) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = comma(round(n_vultures_needed))),
    hjust = -0.15, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", color = "grey15"
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  facet_wrap(~threshold_label, ncol = 3, labeller = threshold_labeller, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = archetype_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = arch_colors) +
  labs(
    title   = "Vultures required to reach outbreak biomass removal thresholds",
    subtitle = "Sole scavenger assumption | Midpoint biomass and intake scenario",
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Vultures needed",
    caption = "Sensitivity range reported in supplementary table. Ceiling applied: fractional birds rounded up."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 14)),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "grey50", hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    strip.text        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10.5),
    strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "#F0F0F0", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.45),
    panel.spacing     = unit(1.4, "lines"),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "grey20"),
    axis.text.x       = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey45"),
    legend.position   = "none"
  )

print(step4_plot)

ggsave(
  file.path(DATADIR, "output_step4_vultures_needed_plot.png"),
  step4_plot, width = 11, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
cat("Saved: output_step4_vultures_needed_plot.png\n")
```
